solve.title: Solve
solve.lead: Type an equation, a system, or anything to work out.
solve.tips: An equation — linear, quadratic, higher powers, fractions, roots, absolute values, exponentials, logarithms — or a system, one equation per line. Or anything without an equals sign: arithmetic with fractions, powers and roots, an expression to simplify, expand or factor, a limit, a derivative or an integral. Every answer is checked.
solve.empty: Type something first — an equation like x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, or something to work out like 1/2 + 1/3.
check.title: Check my working
check.lead: Write your solution one step per line. mathlint finds the first wrong step.
check.tips: Tap the keys or type: / makes a fraction, ^ a power, sqrt, sin, pi and int turn into symbols. Enter starts the next line. Solving an equation? Put it on line 1 and end with x = 2 or x = 3. Ctrl+Enter checks.
workout.title: Work it out
workout.lead: Derivatives, integrals with limits, and matrices, step by step.
workout.boundsNote: Leave both empty for an indefinite integral.
workout.expressionHelp: Tap the keys or type it: x^2 sin x, e^(2x), 1/(x^2+1). The variable is picked up from the expression.
workout.matrixHelp: Write it as [[2, 1], [3, 4]], MATLAB style [2 1; 3 4], or as a LaTeX pmatrix. Fractions stay exact — no decimals.
workout.bothLimits: Fill in both limits for a definite integral, or leave both empty.
report.follows: Every line follows from the one before it.

about.title: About mathlint
about.lead: Type an equation and see it solved step by step — or write out your own working and find your first mistake.
about.private: Everything runs on your device — nothing you type is sent anywhere.
about.checked: Every answer is checked before it is shown. When mathlint is not sure, it says so.
about.support: mathlint is free for personal, educational and other noncommercial use. If it helps you, you can support its development.

about.translationNote: Translations are new: if a step reads oddly, the English original is the reference.
